author: Codex gpt-6.1-sol ultra; no external model

choice_domain.inputs: Only two already legal bank heads before the merged NormalTL first VALID. Never manufacture a head, preempt a walk, increase a native capacity, or reorder an already offered packet.
native_constraints: One FSM/request owner per bank; native AW-before-AR and W overflow guard retained.
bank_read_admit retained, including new-AW same-edge exclusion and FullBufferDID exception only when already legal.
One PTW, IoTLB16, same DDTC/PDTC/native queues and read/write credits.
Identical native hit-bypass, DS-priority configuration, response backpressure, fault routing and full retirement boundary.
No observation of a future PTE/PA, exact future walk length, future unaccepted payload, or hidden MIG queue/direction.

public_snapshot.legal: Per-bank existing legal pending head, immutable header/ttype, exact existing ownership reference if exposed; no arbitrary second head in one bank.
public_snapshot.age: Elapsed from that head's native capture/ready event, with saturation and explicit overflow fallback. Native arrival order is not invented from a bank number.
public_snapshot.current_owner: Existing input W owner and unfilled balance; separately existing output W owner/target and AR/R/B ownership. Different owner domains are not conflated.
public_snapshot.debt: Only bytes/beats and completion obligations already accepted/owned. A blocked obligation is associated with a head only via a certified existing owner/reference dependency, not a task-name guess.
public_snapshot.history: Completed PTW-PTE count and measured accepted-to-retired service samples. Predicted missing PTE count and service time are historical estimates, not the actual future values.
public_snapshot.absence: Absent association means blocked priority=0. Absent required history means RR after the mandatory fair/held checks. A baseline needing a special resource-domain predicate is explicitly inapplicable unless the source/configuration proves it.
public_snapshot.all_rules: All rules can receive the same paid public wires/history. A rule may omit unused hardware and be cheaper; do not force an unused joint predictor onto ordinary control.

order: hold already offered grant/header until native request acceptance
if only one legal head choose it
if a continuously waiting bypassed legal head has the fairness reservation choose it
if the selected algorithm's required history is absent choose native RR
apply the frozen algorithm and then age/RR for ties
common_wrapper.offer: Select and commit bank before merged NormalTL first VALID. Preserve the native 118-bit request exactly except the existing bank tag. No withdraw/change while VALID waits for READY.
common_wrapper.fair: After accepting one selected request while the other head remained continuously waiting and legal, reserve the other head for the next choice at which both are legal. Retain the reservation while it is temporarily ineligible; never retract an offer to honor it. Clear on its acceptance or on source-certified head disappearance/replacement. Fast and slow native accepts both count; walk service itself remains nonpreemptive.
common_wrapper.rr: Existing native RR state advances at actual request acceptance. A missing-history fallback cannot override an already held grant or fairness reservation.
common_wrapper.identity: Bank identities are exchanged with all role/history/owner fields together, never only with the favorable scene label.

algorithms.rule: Choose native RR winner among legal heads. The native two-input RR already implements the one-bypass bound when both heads remain legal; do not add redundant fair storage merely to equalize a bill.

Choose the earlier captured legal head, equivalently greater nonsaturated age. Simultaneous capture uses RR. The common fair reservation overrides FCFS if successive arrivals could otherwise keep the peer waiting.

For each head compute (helps_input_W_owner, helps_output_W_owner, number_of_current_owned_blocked_paths_it_directly_releases). Choose lexicographically descending, then age/RR. All flags/counts use existing owner references; absent certified dependency contributes zero. Do not infer owner assistance just because a head has the same bank as an unrelated W debt.

Choose smaller predicted walk service q_b = last completed slow NormalTL service for the same frozen bank/context/ttype class; break a q tie by smaller last completed PTW-PTE count, then age/RR. Estimates are fixed for both order comparisons and do not change in response to imagined payload service.
Choose smaller D_b = remaining_owned_R_beats + remaining_owned_W_beats + outstanding_owned_B_responses associated with this head. No future descriptors count. Then age/RR.
Choose larger D_b with exactly the same definition as O-debt-min, then age/RR. This is a separate frozen policy, never a scene-dependent switch with O-debt-min.

Let U_b be currently owned remaining R/W/B work directly released by this head and n_b its last completed PTE count. Prefer larger U_b/(1+n_b), using cross multiplication U_0*(1+n_1) versus U_1*(1+n_0), then age/RR. This uses no shared-service rollout. Missing associations give U_b=0; missing n history gives RR.

algorithms.frozen_estimator: On each successful completed owned memory transaction, measure elapsed acceptance-to-retirement divided by beats (ceil, minimum one), classify current payload R or W and preceding completed memory transaction R or W, and overwrite S[previous_class,current_class]. PTW-PTE completions classify as R and are tagged separately for dependency-gap measurement. A W transaction retires at its actual corresponding B boundary, not at W FIFO capture; a read retires at its corresponding last R handshake. The four sample-valid bits must all be true. Estimate tau_RW=max(0,S[R,W]-S[W,W]) and tau_WR=max(0,S[W,R]-S[R,R]); use tau=min(tau_RW,tau_WR). Set g=max(0,last same-walk next_PTE_accept_time minus preceding_PTE_response_time), without subtracting an unobservable queue wait. These are empirical estimates including queue and backpressure, not hidden memory direction or certified causal turnaround.
algorithms.rule: If one legal head is R/RX and one is W and tau>g, choose the R/RX head. Otherwise apply O-short-TL. Common held/fair/missing-history rules remain first. If histories overflow or their context epoch is invalid, use RR. The rule applies online as a heuristic; its exact turnaround theorem applies only to the certified serial-service domain in hand-witness.md.
algorithms.limits: Current drive_ddr serves W and R independently and does not establish the serial-service theorem. Same-ID/held-R/DS constraints and read admission remain unchanged. No runtime peek at MIG internal direction/queue is permitted.
algorithms.kind: complete cheap read/write service-history ordinary control

algorithms.domain: Exactly two ready jobs, translation on one independent serial machine, payload on a distinct independent serial machine, both jobs processed in the same permitted order, no other carried owned service, fixed order-independent t_b and d_b, no read/write owner restriction fixing a conflicting payload order. If any predicate is unproven, this policy uses RR and is labeled inapplicable as a Johnson optimality baseline.
algorithms.rule: For order (i,j) compute C_i=t_i+d_i; C_j=max(t_i+t_j,C_i)+d_j. Choose the order with smaller (C_j,C_i+C_j), then age/RR. Equivalent makespan expression is t_i+max(t_j,d_i)+d_j. This exact two-job enumeration is a complete implementation and avoids assuming Johnson applies beyond its domain.
algorithms.prior_art_scope: Johnson 1954 publisher abstract verifies the known fixed two-stage single-machine-per-stage problem. The above two-job formula is independently derived here. The full original algorithm text was not retrieved; no claim that Johnson covers joint shared-memory feedback is made.
algorithms.kind: exact ordinary fixed two-stage comparison, applicable only when proven

no_posthoc_policy: Every named policy is frozen as a full online rule. A report must name the policy chosen before looking at outcome. Best-of-policy per scene is an offline envelope, not an online competitor; it may bound gains but cannot be called a deployable universal rule.

initial_hand_scope_verdict.turn_positive_neighbor_pair: O-turn exactly reproduces both candidate order decisions in the conditional serial-service pair; that pair is not a difference-gate witness.
initial_hand_scope_verdict.native_turn_pair: Ineligible: current drive_ddr has independent W/R service, and native dual-head/read admission reachability is not established for the hand schedule.
initial_hand_scope_verdict.joint_kernel_family: Open. A cheap rule covering one pair is not proof of full family equivalence or published prior-art coverage.
initial_hand_scope_verdict.fixed_independent_two_stage: If source proves this domain, joint prediction with the same fixed t/d reduces exactly to O-two-stage for these two jobs; do not claim joint prediction is independently new there.
